questions.question: A product is originally priced at ₹2,000. A 15% discount is applied to the original price. After the discount, a 10% Value Added Tax (VAT) is charged on the discounted price. What is the net amount paid for the product?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Original price = ₹2000

Discount = 15%

VAT = 10%

**Formula used:**

Discounted price = MP − Discount

Final price = Discounted price + VAT

**Calculation:**

Discount = 2000 × 15 ÷ 100 = 300

Price after discount = 2000 − 300 = 1700

VAT = 1700 × 10 ÷ 100 = 170

Final amount = 1700 + 170 = 1870

**∴ Net amount paid = ₹1870.**

questions.question: **Fill in the blanks**: A Bill that "imposes a new tax" is categorised at the Centre as a ______ Bill.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__
 
__ 
 
• A **Money Bill** is a type of bill in the Indian Parliament that exclusively deals with matters specified in **Article 110** of the Constitution of India. 
 
• It includes provisions for the imposition, abolition, remission, alteration, or regulation of any **tax or revenue** collection. 
 
• Under Article 110, a bill is classified as a Money Bill if it deals with: 
 
 
• The imposition or abolition of taxes. 
 
• The custody and withdrawal of money from the **Consolidated Fund of India** or the **Contingency Fund of India**. 
 
• The appropriation of money out of the Consolidated Fund. 
 
 
 
• A Money Bill can only be introduced in the **Lok Sabha**, not in the Rajya Sabha. 
 
• After being passed by the Lok Sabha, the Rajya Sabha can only suggest amendments, which the Lok Sabha may accept or reject. The Rajya Sabha cannot reject or amend a Money Bill without the concurrence of the Lok Sabha. 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 
__ 
 
• **Ordinary Bill:** 
 
 
• An Ordinary Bill is a regular bill that deals with any matter other than financial matters specified under Article 110. 
 
• It can be introduced in either the **Lok Sabha** or the **Rajya Sabha**. 
 
• It requires the approval of both houses and has no special financial provisions. 
 
 
 
• **Private Bill:** 
 
 
• A Private Bill is introduced by a **private member** (a Member of Parliament who is not a minister). 
 
• It deals with public interest issues but is rarely passed in the Indian Parliament. 
 
 
 
• **Constitutional Amendment Bill:** 
 
 
• It is introduced to amend the provisions of the **Constitution of India** under Article 368. 
 
• It requires a special majority in both houses of Parliament and, in some cases, the ratification of half of the state legislatures. 
 
 
 
• **Procedure for a Money Bill:** 
 
 
• The Speaker of the Lok Sabha decides whether a bill is a Money Bill or not, and the decision is final. 
 
• After passage in the Lok Sabha, the Money Bill is sent to the Rajya Sabha, which must return it within **14 days**. 
 
• If the Rajya Sabha fails to return the bill within 14 days, it is deemed to have been passed by both houses in the form in which it was passed by the Lok Sabha. 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
 
 
• **Article 110:** It lays down the definition of a Money Bill in the Indian Constitution. 
 
• **Role of the Speaker:** The Speaker of the Lok Sabha has the final authority to decide whether a bill is a Money Bill or not. 
 
• **Exclusive Introduction:** Money Bills can only be introduced in the Lok Sabha on the recommendation of the **President of India**. 
 
• **Examples:** The **Finance Bill** and the **Appropriation Bill** are types of Money Bills.

questions.question: The moment of inertia of a rigid body about an axis:

The correct answer is __**Is a scalar quantity, dependent on the axis**__.

__ 

• The **moment of inertia** of a rigid body is a measure of its resistance to angular acceleration when a torque is applied about an axis. 

• **Moment of inertia** is a scalar quantity and depends on the **distribution of mass** in the rigid body and the **specific axis** about which it is being calculated. 

• It is calculated mathematically as the **integral of mass elements multiplied by the square of their perpendicular distances** from the axis of rotation (**I = ∫r² dm**). 

• The value of the moment of inertia changes based on the **geometry, shape, and orientation** of the body relative to the axis. For example, the moment of inertia of a rod about its center is different from that about one of its ends. 

• *Hence, the moment of inertia is a scalar quantity, but it is **dependent on the axis**.* 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 
__ 

• **Definition of Moment of Inertia:** 
 

• The moment of inertia represents the rotational equivalent of mass in linear motion. It quantifies how the mass is distributed relative to the axis of rotation. 

• Its SI unit is **kg.m²**, and it is always a positive scalar quantity. 
 
 

• **Factors Affecting Moment of Inertia:** 
 

• **Mass Distribution:** The farther the mass is from the axis, the greater the moment of inertia. 

• **Axis of Rotation:** The axis's location and orientation significantly affect the value of the moment of inertia. For example, a uniform disc has different moments of inertia when rotated about its central axis and its diameter. 

• **Shape and Geometry:** The shape (sphere, cylinder, rod, etc.) of the object influences its moment of inertia. 
 
 

• **Applications of Moment of Inertia:** 
 

• It is crucial in **mechanical systems** involving rotation, such as flywheels and turbines. 

• In the design of vehicles, it helps determine the **stability and control** of rotating components like wheels and propellers. 

• It is also used in **structural engineering** to analyze beams and other elements subject to torque or rotational forces. 
 
 

• **Parallel and Perpendicular Axis Theorems:** 
 

• **Parallel Axis Theorem:** If the moment of inertia of a body about an axis passing through its center of mass is known, the moment of inertia about any parallel axis can be calculated as **I = I_cm + Md²**, where d is the distance between the axes. 

• **Perpendicular Axis Theorem:** For a planar body, the moment of inertia about an axis perpendicular to the plane is the sum of the moments of inertia about two mutually perpendicular axes in the plane. 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
 

• **Moment of Inertia for Common Shapes:** 
 

• **Thin Rod:** About an axis through the center and perpendicular to its length: **I = (1/12)ML²**. 

• **Solid Sphere:** About its diameter: **I = (2/5)MR²**. 

• **Solid Cylinder:** About its central axis: **I = (1/2)MR²**. 

• **Hollow Cylinder:** About its central axis: **I = MR²**. 
 
 

• The **moment of inertia** is an integral property that underpins key concepts in rotational dynamics, such as angular momentum and torque. 

• It is not a vector quantity but a scalar, although its influence is directional based on the axis of rotation. 

• Understanding the moment of inertia is essential in designing efficient mechanical systems and analyzing rotational motion in physics.

• The revenue budget details the government’s recurring expenditures on areas such as **administration, subsidies, pensions, interest payments, and defense expenditure**. 
 
• When revenue receipts exceed revenue expenditure, it results in a **Revenue Surplus**. Conversely, when the expenditure surpasses receipts, it leads to a **Revenue Deficit**. 
 
• It differs from the **Capital Budget**, which deals with long-term investments and liabilities, focusing on creating assets like infrastructure. 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Capital Budget:** 
 
 
• Deals with the government’s revenue from loans, borrowings, and the creation of assets like roads, schools, and hospitals. 
 
• Includes capital receipts (e.g., loans, recovery of loans, disinvestment) and capital expenditure (e.g., infrastructure development). 
 
 
 
• **Finance Budget:** 
 
 
• It refers to the overall annual financial statement presented in Parliament, containing details of both revenue and capital budgets. 
 
• It is an umbrella term encompassing all aspects of the government’s financial planning. 
 
 
 
• **Expenditure Budget:** 
 
 
• It is a part of the Union Budget that provides a detailed account of the government’s expenditure for the fiscal year. 
 
• It is divided into revenue expenditure and capital expenditure. 
 
 
 
• **Revenue Receipts:** 
 
 
• Comprises tax revenues (e.g., GST, customs duties) and non-tax revenues (e.g., dividends, interest receipts). 
 
• These receipts do not lead to an increase in liabilities or a reduction in assets. 
 
 
 
• **Revenue Expenditure:** 
 
 
• Includes day-to-day operational expenses such as salaries, subsidies, and interest payments. 
 
• Unlike capital expenditure, it does not result in the creation of assets or reduction of liabilities.

• **Revenue Budget:** Focuses on recurring income and expenditure, does not create assets. 
 
• **Capital Budget:** Focuses on long-term investments, asset creation, and liabilities. 
 
 
 
• **Revenue Deficit:** Occurs when revenue expenditure exceeds revenue receipts, indicating a shortfall in meeting day-to-day expenses. 
 
• **Budget Presentation:** In India, the Union Budget is presented annually by the Finance Minister, as mandated under **Article 112** of the Indian Constitution. 
 
• **Key Components of Union Budget:** Revenue Budget, Capital Budget, Finance Bill, and Appropriation Bill.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Industrial Policy Resolution (IPR) of 1956** was a landmark in India’s economic policy, laying the foundation of a mixed economy where both the public and private sectors could co-exist under state regulation.
 
• The government introduced licensing even for expansion of private industries to maintain **control over production capacity** and ensure that resources were allocated based on national priorities.
 
• The licensing system aimed to regulate the growth of certain industries, ensuring that they aligned with the **development goals of the government**, such as equitable distribution of resources and prevention of monopolies.
 
• This measure was implemented to ensure that the private sector did not dominate critical industries and that the state maintained a significant role in economic planning and resource allocation.
 
• The focus was particularly on industries considered critical for national development, such as **steel, heavy machinery, and defense**, which were placed under stringent control to meet long-term goals.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Industrial Policy Resolution (IPR) of 1956:**
 
 
• The IPR 1956 categorized industries into three schedules:
 
 
• **Schedule A:** Industries exclusively reserved for the public sector, such as defense and atomic energy.
 
• **Schedule B:** Industries where both the public and private sectors could operate, but the government took an active role.
 
• **Schedule C:** Industries left to the private sector but regulated by the government through licensing.
 
 
 
• The policy emphasized the importance of the public sector in commanding the economy and achieving **socialist-inspired goals** of equitable distribution of wealth.
 
 
 
• **Objectives of Licensing:**
 
 
• To prevent excessive concentration of economic power in a few hands and ensure **balanced regional development**.
 
• To prioritize the allocation of resources to industries crucial for the country’s development, such as infrastructure and heavy industries.
 
• To regulate production to meet domestic demands and prevent overproduction or underproduction in specific sectors.
 
 
 
• **Impact of Licensing:**
 
 
• The licensing system led to the emergence of the **License Raj**, where businesses had to obtain multiple clearances and approvals, often leading to inefficiencies and corruption.
 
• While the system aimed to ensure equitable growth, it also hindered innovation and competitiveness in the private sector.
 
• The government retained significant control over industrial growth, aligning production with its planned economic goals.
 
 
 
• **Alternatives to Licensing:**
 
 
• In the 1991 economic reforms, the government dismantled the License Raj, allowing industries to grow freely with fewer restrictions.
 
• This liberalization policy aimed to boost **economic efficiency, innovation, and competitiveness** in the global market.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

Consider the following statements:

1. Article 263 empowers Parliament to establish Inter-State Council.

2. The Council can investigate inter-state disputes.

3. Its composition includes PM and Union Ministers.

Which of the above is/are **correct**?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**4) 2 and 3**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Article 263 of the Constitution of India empowers the President, not Parliament, to establish the Inter-State Council. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• The **Inter-State Council** is tasked with investigating and discussing subjects of common interest between states or between the Union and states. It also makes recommendations for better coordination of policy and action on such subjects. ***Hence, statement 2 is correct.***
 
• The composition of the **Inter-State Council** includes the **Prime Minister as the Chairperson**, Union Ministers, and Chief Ministers of states. It is structured to ensure representation from all levels of government. ***Hence, statement 3 is correct.***
 
• The Council's role is consultative, and it does not have adjudicatory or binding decision-making power over inter-state disputes.
 
• **Article 263** does not mandate the creation of an Inter-State Council but leaves it to the discretion of the President, based on the necessity for coordination and cooperation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Constitutional Provision (Article 263):**

 
 
• Article 263 of the Constitution provides for the establishment of an **Inter-State Council** to serve as a platform for discussion and resolution of disputes between states or between states and the Union.
 
• The article outlines three main purposes of the council: **investigating inter-state disputes, discussing subjects of common interest, and making recommendations** for coordination of policy and action.
 
• The Council is consultative in nature and does not have binding authority.
 
 
 
• **Composition of the Inter-State Council:**
 
 
• The **Prime Minister** serves as the Chairperson of the Council.
 
• Other members include **Chief Ministers of all states, Administrators of Union Territories, and Union Ministers** as designated by the Prime Minister.
 
 
 
• **Inter-State Council's Functions:**
 
 
• Facilitates coordination between states and the Union in areas of mutual interest.
 
• Provides recommendations for better policy implementation and dispute resolution.
 
• Investigates and discusses specific issues referred to it by the President.
 
 
 
• **Significance of the Council:**
 
 
• Helps in promoting cooperative federalism by providing a platform for dialogue between states and the Union.
 
• Addresses administrative and legislative challenges in a non-adjudicative manner.
 
• Encourages harmonization of policies across states for common goals such as economic growth and social development.
 
 
 
• **Historical Context:**
 
 
• The Inter-State Council was established in **1990** by a Presidential Order based on the recommendations of the **Sarkaria Commission**.
 
• The Sarkaria Commission emphasized the need for such a forum to improve Centre-State and inter-state relations.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Role of the Inter-State Council:** It is purely advisory in nature and does not have the power to adjudicate disputes or enforce its recommendations.
 
• **Sarkaria Commission:** Recommended the establishment of the Inter-State Council to address Centre-State and inter-state conflicts and enhance cooperative federalism.
 
• **Article 262 vs. Article 263:** While **Article 262** deals with the adjudication of inter-state water disputes, **Article 263** focuses on a consultative mechanism for broader inter-state issues.
 
• **Cooperative Federalism:** The council is an essential mechanism for fostering dialogue and collaboration between states and the Union, promoting the ideal of cooperative federalism enshrined in the Constitution.

questions.question: Which of the following is a non-zero number that belongs to every set: Whole, Integer, Rational, and Real?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Every Whole number is automatically an Integer, a Rational number, and a Real number.

The set of Whole numbers is {0, 1, 2, 3, ...}.

We need a non-zero number, which eliminates 0.

Among the given options, only 1 is a non-zero whole number.

**∴ The correct answer is 1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Sets to check: Whole, Integer, Rational, and Real numbers.

Condition: The number must be non-zero.

**Definitions:**

⇒ Whole numbers = {0, 1, 2, 3, ...}

⇒ Integers = {..., −2, −1, 0, 1, 2, ...}

⇒ Rational numbers = Numbers of the form p/q (where q ≠ 0).

⇒ Real numbers = All rational and irrational numbers.

**Checking the Options:**

⇒ Option 1: 1 is non-zero. It is a Whole number, Integer, Rational (1/1), and Real. (Satisfies all)

⇒ Option 2: 0 is a Whole number, but the question asks for a non-zero number. (Rejected)

⇒ Option 3: −1 is an Integer but NOT a Whole number. (Rejected)

⇒ Option 4: √2 is a Real number but NOT a Whole, Integer, or Rational number. (Rejected)

**∴ The correct answer is 1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Natural Numbers

Counting numbers starting from 1 are called Natural numbers (N = {1, 2, 3, 4, ...}). They do not include 0, fractions, or decimals.

Irrational Numbers

Numbers that cannot be written as a simple fraction p/q. Their decimal expansions are non-terminating and non-repeating. Examples: √2, π, e.

Prime Numbers

Natural numbers greater than 1 that have exactly two distinct positive divisors: 1 and themselves. Examples: 2, 3, 5, 7, 11.

questions.question: Partners X and Y entered into a business investing Rs. 50,000 and Rs. 1,00,000 respectively. After 6 months, Z joins with Rs. 1,50,000. At year-end, profit was Rs. 90,000. How much more did Z earn than X?

Profit ratio is directly proportional to (Capital × Time).

Ratio = 600 : 1200 : 900 = 2 : 4 : 3

Total profit = 2 + 4 + 3 = 9 parts = Rs. 90,000 ⇒ 1 part = Rs. 10,000

Difference in earnings of Z and X = 3 − 2 = 1 part.

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 10,000.**

Profit Ratio = (C₁ × T₁) : (C₂ × T₂) : (C₃ × T₃)

 
• X 50k 12 mths Ratio: 2 Y 100k 12 mths Ratio: 4 Z 150k 6 mths Ratio: 3 
 Diff (Z − X) = 3 − 2 = 1 part

⇒ Time period for X = 12 months

⇒ Time period for Y = 12 months

⇒ Z joined after 6 months, so Time period for Z = 12 − 6 = 6 months

⇒ Profit Ratio (X : Y : Z) = (50,000 × 12) : (1,00,000 × 12) : (1,50,000 × 6)

⇒ Ratio = 6,00,000 : 12,00,000 : 9,00,000

⇒ 9 parts = Rs. 90,000

⇒ Profit share of X = 2 × 10,000 = Rs. 20,000

⇒ Profit share of Z = 3 × 10,000 = Rs. 30,000

⇒ Difference (Z − X) = 30,000 − 20,000 = Rs. 10,000

questions.question: A person invested in two items — one gave a 10% profit and the other a 5% loss. If the total investment was Rs. 5,000 and the net result was a Rs. 100 profit, what was the investment in the profit-making item?

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Overall profit percentage = (100 ÷ 5000) × 100 = +2%

By Alligation, ratio of profit to loss investment = (2 − (−5)) : (10 − 2) = 7 : 8

Total investment parts = 7 + 8 = 15 parts

Investment in profit item = (7 ÷ 15) × 5000 ⇒ 35000 ÷ 15 = 2333.33

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 2,333.33.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Total Investment = Rs. 5000

Profit on 1st item = 10%

Loss on 2nd item = 5%

Net profit = Rs. 100

**Formula Used:**

Net Profit = (Profit on 1st item) − (Loss on 2nd item)

 
• 
• 
• 
• Profit Item Loss Item +10% −5% +2% 7 8 Ratio = 7 : 8 

**Calculations:**

Let the investment in the profit-making item be x.

⇒ Investment in the loss-making item = 5000 − x

⇒ Profit from 1st item = 10% of x = 0.10x

⇒ Loss from 2nd item = 5% of (5000 − x) = 0.05 × (5000 − x)

⇒ Net profit = 0.10x − 0.05 × (5000 − x)

⇒ 100 = 0.10x − 250 + 0.05x

⇒ 100 + 250 = 0.15x

⇒ 350 = 0.15x

⇒ x = 350 ÷ 0.15

⇒ x = 35000 ÷ 15

⇒ x = 7000 ÷ 3 ≈ 2333.33

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 2,333.33.**

questions.question: A group of 5 men or 12 women can complete a task in 70 days. Find the time taken by 5 men and 12 women to complete the task.

Time = 35 days

questions.question: A machine can fill 120 milk bottles in 6 minutes. How many milk bottles can it fill in 14 minutes?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Using the unitary method, we can first find the number of bottles filled in 1 minute.

Bottles filled per minute = 120 ÷ 6 = 20 bottles.

Bottles filled in 14 minutes = 20 × 14 = 280 bottles.

**∴ The correct answer is 280 milk bottles.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial work (W₁) = 120 bottles

Initial time (T₁) = 6 minutes

New time (T₂) = 14 minutes

**Formula Used:**

Using the chain rule for direct proportion: W₁ / T₁ = W₂ / T₂

 6 minutes 
 
 × 20 (Rate) 120 bottles 14 minutes 
 
 × 20 (Rate) 280 bottles 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 120 / 6 = W₂ / 14

⇒ 20 = W₂ / 14

⇒ W₂ = 20 × 14

⇒ W₂ = 280

**∴ The correct answer is 280 milk bottles.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Direct Proportion

When two quantities increase or decrease together, they are in direct proportion. The ratio of their values remains constant: X₁ / Y₁ = X₂ / Y₂.

Inverse Proportion

When one quantity increases while the other decreases, they are in inverse proportion. Their product remains constant: X₁ × Y₁ = X₂ × Y₂.

Unitary Method

A technique to solve proportion problems by first finding the value of a single unit, and then multiplying that rate to find the required proportional value.

questions.question: The average weight of 10 boxes is 15.5 kg. If the heaviest box weighs 21 kg and the lightest weighs 10 kg, what is the average weight of the remaining boxes?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Average weight of the two removed boxes = (21 + 10) ÷ 2 = 15.5 kg.

If the average of the removed items is exactly equal to the original average of the group, the new average remains unchanged.

Since the removed boxes have the same average as the whole group, there is 0 net deviation.

**∴ The correct answer is 15.5 kg.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Average weight of 10 boxes = 15.5 kg

Weight of the heaviest box = 21 kg

Weight of the lightest box = 10 kg

**Formula Used:**

Sum of observations = Average × Number of observations

 
• 
• 
• Total 10 boxes = 155 kg (15.5 kg/box) 10 kg Remaining 8 boxes (124 kg) 21 kg 
• 
• 
• New Average = 124 ÷ 8 = 15.5 kg 
• 
• 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total weight of 10 boxes = 10 × 15.5 = 155 kg

⇒ Total weight of the heaviest and lightest boxes = 21 + 10 = 31 kg

⇒ Weight of the remaining 8 boxes = 155 − 31 = 124 kg

⇒ Average weight of the remaining boxes = 124 ÷ 8

⇒ Average weight = 15.5 kg

**∴ The correct answer is 15.5 kg.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Net Deviation Method

If the average of a sub-group removed from a total group is perfectly equal to the original average, the new average remains unchanged.

Combined Average

When combining two separate groups, the combined average is represented by: (n₁A₁ + n₂A₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂).

Replacement in Average

New value = Old value + (Number of items × Change in average). A positive change means the incoming item is heavier.

questions.question: A mixture of 150 litres contains acid and water in the ratio 2:3. If 30 litres of the mixture is replaced with water, what will be the percentage of acid in the final mixture?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Initial acid percentage in the mixture = (2 / 5) × 100 = 40%

Fraction of original mixture remaining = (150 − 30) / 150 = 120 / 150 = 4 / 5

Since the removed part is replaced by pure water, the acid concentration reduces proportionally.

Final acid percentage = Initial % × Fraction remaining = 40% × (4 / 5) = 32%

**∴ The correct answer is 32%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total initial volume of mixture = 150 litres

Ratio of acid to water = 2 : 3

Amount of mixture replaced with water = 30 litres

 
 
 150 Litres Ratio 2:3 Acid: 60L Water: 90L 
• − 30L Mixture 
• + 30L Water 150 Litres Acid: 48L Water: 102L Acid = 32% 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Quantity of acid initially = [2 / (2 + 3)] × 150 = (2 / 5) × 150 = 60 litres

⇒ When 30 litres of mixture is removed, the acid removed proportionally = (2 / 5) × 30 = 12 litres

⇒ Remaining acid in the mixture = 60 − 12 = 48 litres

⇒ Total volume after replacing with 30 litres of water remains 150 litres

⇒ Percentage of acid in final mixture = (Remaining Acid / Total Volume) × 100

⇒ Percentage of acid = (48 / 150) × 100 = 32%

**∴ The correct answer is 32%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Replacement Formula

If a vessel contains V litres of pure liquid, and R litres are repeatedly removed and replaced with another liquid n times, the remaining pure liquid = V × (1 − R/V)ⁿ.

Alligation Rule

Ratio of quantities = (Cheaper quantity / Dearer quantity) = (Price of dearer − Mean price) / (Mean price − Price of cheaper). This easily computes mixture proportions.

Concentration in Mixtures

When two mixtures of volumes V₁ and V₂ with concentrations C₁ and C₂ are mixed, the final concentration is (C₁V₁ + C₂V₂) ÷ (V₁ + V₂).

questions.question: A water tank is shaped like a composite prism: the bottom part is a triangular prism with base area 60 cm² and height 1.2 m, while the top part is a rectangular prism with base 40 cm × 30 cm and height 0.8 m. What is the total volume of the tank in liters? (1 m³ = 1000 L)
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Convert all heights to cm: 0.8 m = 80 cm and 1.2 m = 120 cm.

Volume of top part = Length × Width × Height = 40 × 30 × 80 = 96,000 cm³ = 96 L.

Volume of bottom part = Base Area × Height = 60 × 120 = 7,200 cm³ = 7.2 L.

Total Volume = 96 L + 7.2 L = 103.2 L.

**∴ The correct answer is 103.2 L.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Base dimensions of the top rectangular prism = 40 cm × 30 cm

Height of the top rectangular prism = 0.8 m = 80 cm

Base area of the bottom triangular prism = 60 cm²

Height of the bottom triangular prism = 1.2 m = 120 cm

**Formula Used:**

Volume of a rectangular prism = Length × Width × Height

Volume of any prism = Base Area × Height

1 Liter (L) = 1,000 cm³

 
 Top Part (Rectangular Prism) Base = 40 × 30 cm, Height = 80 cm Volume = 96,000 cu cm = 96 L Bottom Part (Triangular Prism) Base Area = 60 sq cm, Height = 120 cm Volume = 7,200 cu cm = 7.2 L Total Volume = 96 L + 7.2 L = 103.2 L 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Volume of the top rectangular part = 40 × 30 × 80

⇒ Volume of the top rectangular part = 96,000 cm³

⇒ Convert top part to liters: 96,000 ÷ 1000 = 96 L

⇒ Volume of the bottom triangular part = 60 × 120

⇒ Volume of the bottom triangular part = 7,200 cm³

⇒ Convert bottom part to liters: 7,200 ÷ 1000 = 7.2 L

⇒ Total capacity of the water tank = 96 L + 7.2 L = 103.2 L

**∴ The correct answer is 103.2 L.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Volume of a Prism

The volume of any prism is calculated by the product of its uniform base area and its height (V = Base Area × Height), regardless of the geometric shape of its base.

Important Volume Conversions

1 m³ = 1,000 Liters and 1 Liter = 1,000 cm³. By relation, 1 m³ equals 1,000,000 cm³.

Composite Solids

The total volume of a composite figure is simply the direct sum of the volumes of its individual 3D components without any geometric loss.

questions.question: If cotA = x + ((1)/(x)), then what is cosec²A?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The standard trigonometric identity is cosec²A = 1 + cot²A.

Substitute cotA = x + (1/x) directly into the formula.

cosec²A = 1 + [x + (1/x)]²

cosec²A = 1 + x² + (1/x²) + 2

cosec²A = x² + (1/x²) + 3

**∴ The correct answer is x² + (1/x²) + 3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

cotA = x + (1/x)

**Formula Used:**

cosec²A − cot²A = 1

(a + b)² = a² + b² + 2ab

**Calculations:**

⇒ cosec²A = 1 + cot²A

⇒ cosec²A = 1 + [x + (1/x)]²

⇒ cosec²A = 1 + x² + (1/x)² + 2 × x × (1/x)

⇒ cosec²A = 1 + x² + (1/x²) + 2

⇒ cosec²A = x² + (1/x²) + 3

**∴ The correct answer is x² + (1/x²) + 3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Pythagorean Trigonometric Identities

• sin²θ + cos²θ = 1

• sec²θ − tan²θ = 1

• cosec²θ − cot²θ = 1

Reciprocal Trigonometric Identities

• sinθ = 1 ÷ cosecθ

• cosθ = 1 ÷ secθ

• tanθ = 1 ÷ cotθ

Standard Algebraic Identity

• (a + b)² = a² + b² + 2ab

questions.question: Find slope of the line passing through points (-2,5) and (4,-7).
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The slope of a straight line passing through any two given points is calculated directly by the ratio of the change in y to the change in x.

Slope = Change in y ÷ Change in x

Slope = (−7 − 5) ÷ (4 − (−2))

Slope = −12 ÷ 6 = −2

**∴ The correct answer is −2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Coordinates of the first point: (x₁, y₁) = (−2, 5)

Coordinates of the second point: (x₂, y₂) = (4, −7)

**Formula Used:**

Slope (m) = (y₂ − y₁) ÷ (x₂ − x₁)

 
• 
• X Y O 
• 
• 
• Δx = 6 Δy = −12 (−2, 5) (4, −7) m = −12 ÷ 6 = −2 

**Calculations:**

⇒ m = (−7 − 5) ÷ (4 − (−2))

⇒ m = −12 ÷ (4 + 2)

⇒ m = −12 ÷ 6

⇒ m = −2

**∴ The correct answer is −2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Equation of a Line (Two-Point Form)

The equation of a straight line passing through (x₁, y₁) and (x₂, y₂) is given by y − y₁ = m(x − x₁), where m is the slope.

Parallel and Perpendicular Lines

Two lines are considered parallel if their slopes are equal (m₁ = m₂) and perpendicular if the product of their slopes is −1 (m₁ × m₂ = −1).

Distance Formula

The straight-line distance between two points (x₁, y₁) and (x₂, y₂) is d = √[(x₂ − x₁)² + (y₂ − y₁)²].

questions.question: What is the minimum distance from the origin (0,0) to a point on the line segment connecting the points A(3, 0) and B(0, 4)?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The points A(3, 0), B(0, 4) and Origin O(0, 0) form a right-angled triangle.

The minimum distance from the origin to the line segment AB is simply the altitude drawn to the hypotenuse.

Altitude (h) = (Base × Perpendicular) ÷ Hypotenuse

Here, Base = 3, Perpendicular = 4, Hypotenuse = √(3² + 4²) = 5.

h = (3 × 4) ÷ 5 = 12 ÷ 5 = 2.4

**∴ The correct answer is 2.4 units.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Origin O = (0, 0), Point A = (3, 0) and Point B = (0, 4)

**Formula Used:**

Area of right-angled triangle = 1/2 × base × height

Hypotenuse = √(base² + height²)

 
• 
• 
 
• 
 
 O(0, 0) A(3, 0) B(0, 4) 3 4 AB = 5 h h = (3 × 4) ÷ 5 = 2.4 units 

**Calculations:**

⇒ OA = 3 units and OB = 4 units

⇒ In ΔOAB, Hypotenuse AB = √(OA² + OB²)

⇒ AB = √(3² + 4²) = √(9 + 16) = √25 = 5 units

⇒ The minimum distance from origin O to line AB is the perpendicular altitude (h) from O to AB.

⇒ Area of ΔOAB = 1/2 × base × height = 1/2 × OA × OB

⇒ Area of ΔOAB = 1/2 × 3 × 4 = 6 sq. units

⇒ Using AB as the base, Area of ΔOAB = 1/2 × AB × h

⇒ 1/2 × 5 × h = 6

⇒ 5 × h = 12

⇒ h = 12 ÷ 5 = 2.4 units

**∴ The correct answer is 2.4 units.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Perpendicular Distance from Origin

The perpendicular distance from the origin (0, 0) to any straight line given by the equation ax + by + c = 0 is determined using the formula d = |c| ÷ √(a² + b²).

Altitude to Hypotenuse

In any right-angled triangle with base 'a', perpendicular 'b' and hypotenuse 'c', the length of the altitude drawn to the hypotenuse is h = (a × b) ÷ c.

Line Intercept Form

The standard equation of a straight line making an x-intercept 'a' and a y-intercept 'b' on the coordinate axes is x/a + y/b = 1.

questions.question: If in △LMN and △OPQ, ∠L=∠O, LM = OP, and ∠M=∠P, which rule proves △LMN≅△OPQ?

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Identify the position of the given equal parts in △LMN and △OPQ:

1. ∠L = ∠O (Angle)

2. LM = OP (Included Side)

3. ∠M = ∠P (Angle)

Since the equal side is positioned exactly between the two equal angles, the triangles are congruent by the ASA (Angle-Side-Angle) rule.

**∴ The correct answer is ASA.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

⇒ In △LMN and △OPQ, ∠L = ∠O, LM = OP, and ∠M = ∠P

 
 L M N 
 
 
 
• 
 O P Q 
 
 
 
• 

**Step-by-step Proof:**

⇒ ∠L = ∠O (Given equal angles)

⇒ LM = OP (Given equal included sides)

⇒ ∠M = ∠P (Given equal angles)

⇒ When two angles and the included side of one triangle are equal to the corresponding two angles and included side of another triangle, the two triangles are defined as congruent.

⇒ Therefore, by the Angle-Side-Angle (ASA) property, △LMN ≅ △OPQ.

**∴ The correct answer is ASA.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

SAS (Side-Angle-Side) Congruence

Two triangles are congruent if two sides and the included angle of one are equal to the corresponding sides and included angle of the other.

SSS (Side-Side-Side) Congruence

Two triangles are congruent if all three sides of one triangle are respectively equal to the three sides of the other.

AAS (Angle-Angle-Side) Congruence

Two triangles are congruent if any two angles and a non-included side of one are equal to the corresponding parts of the other.

RHS (Right Angle-Hypotenuse-Side) Congruence

Two right-angled triangles are congruent if the hypotenuse and one side of one triangle are equal to the hypotenuse and corresponding side of the other.

⇒ ∠AOB = 60°

questions.question: You earn 52.50 in 3.5 hours. Find your hourly wage as a fraction.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Hourly Wage = Total Earnings ÷ Total Hours

⇒ Hourly Wage = 52.50 ÷ 3.5

⇒ Multiply by 10 to clear decimals: 525 ÷ 35

⇒ 525 ÷ 35 = 15

⇒ As a fraction: 15/1

**∴ The correct answer is 15/1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total Earnings = 52.50

Total Time = 3.5 hours

**Formula Used:**

Hourly Wage = Total Earnings ÷ Total Time

**Calculations:**

⇒ Hourly Wage = 52.50 ÷ 3.5

⇒ To remove the decimal point, multiply the numerator and the denominator by 10.

⇒ Hourly Wage = (52.50 × 10) ÷ (3.5 × 10)

⇒ Hourly Wage = 525 ÷ 35

⇒ Simplify by dividing both terms by 5:
